open_points.subject: A10 rule 7 request_digest header set
open_points.text: "the request an approval covers is described ... by: ... every header the kernel sends ... each with its value"
open_points.question: Which headers are included in the approval digest: only headers explicitly set by kernel rules (required headers, credential header name, content-type, accept-encoding), or also transport/client-added headers such as Host, Content-Length, User-Agent, and multipart boundary-dependent header values?
options: Include only headers explicitly defined by Cabinet rules
Include the full on-wire header set after HTTP client finalization
open_points.default_guess: Include only explicitly defined kernel headers, to keep approval stability and determinism.

open_points.subject: A11 rule 4 recovery marking authority-used
open_points.text: "marks the approval the attempt names as its authority `used`" together with M26 "authority: the approval or the grant it used, or for a `draft-write` send the flow activation"
open_points.question: On restart recovery of an `in_flight` attempt whose authority was a standing grant or flow activation (not an approval), what exact state change is required for authority usage bookkeeping?
options: No extra authority state change when authority is not an approval
Introduce/use a 'used' notion for grants/flow-activation authority records
open_points.default_guess: Apply 'used' transition only when authority is an approval; do nothing for grant/flow-activation authority.

open_points.subject: K-02 filesystem prohibition vs A03 sandbox filesystem allowance
open_points.text: K-02: "no filesystem beyond its input" vs A03 rule 1: "one private exchange directory ... opening any path outside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime"
open_points.question: Are function implementations allowed to perform filesystem I/O inside the sandbox exchange directory, or should all filesystem I/O be forbidden and data passed only in-memory?
options: Allow I/O only inside exchange directory (as A03 implies)
Forbid all filesystem I/O to match strict reading of K-02
open_points.default_guess: Allow only exchange-directory I/O, treating K-02 as 'no host/application filesystem access'.
